Patient-Reported Drug Review Analytics & Ranking

Condition-Stratified Drug Ranking Using Bayesian Shrinkage and Interactive Analytics. Real Drugs.com reviews, cleaned, ranked with a shrinkage estimator, checked for stability and temporal drift, and bounded by an explicit validity analysis.

Search a conditionShrinkage sensitivityValidation

Methodology

How raw scraped reviews became comparable numbers.

1Combine

Train and test files merged: raw rows.

2Clean

Dropped rows with no condition and scraped artifacts ("users found this comment helpful") that landed in the condition column.

3Normalise

Trimmed and title-cased conditions, decoded HTML entities in reviews.

4Aggregate

One row per condition + drug pair (8,586): review count, mean rating, mean helpful votes and the full 1–10 rating histogram. These sufficient statistics drive everything below, so updates are instant.

5Score

Shrink each drug's mean toward its condition's mean (empirical-Bayes style, strength m you can change) so tiny samples cannot win.

6Validate

Split reviews into random halves and check the two drug rankings agree (split-half Spearman ρ) across 89 conditions.

7Diagnose

Inspect rating histograms and year-by-year drift, since averages alone hide polarisation and non-stationarity.

8Bound & serve

State what the data cannot support, then serve the precomputed statistics client-side so every view is interactive.

Protocol

  • Every figure on this page is computed from the real files, nothing is simulated.
  • Drugs are only ranked against others reviewed for the same condition.
  • Rank by the weighted score, never by raw mean alone; always read the review count beside it.
  • Most-helpful reviews are shown verbatim (trimmed) so you can sanity-check the numbers.

Why a weighted score computed live

A drug with three 10/10 reviews should not outrank one with 900 reviews averaging 9.

Condition mean C = (average of all reviews in this dataset). Weighted = n/(n+m)·mean + m/(n+m)·C.

Raw mean
Weighted score

Weight placed on a drug's own mean

Weight = n/(n+m). With m = 10 a drug needs about 10 reviews before its own data counts for half, and at 100 reviews it counts for 91%. Larger m shrinks harder.

Signature analyses new

Two views that go beyond averages and rankings.

Love-or-Hate map

Love-or-Hate Index = 4 · P(rating ≤ 3) · P(rating ≥ 8). It is 0 when reviewers agree and 1 when they split evenly between hating and loving a drug. Dots are drugs with ≥100 reviews; size = review count. Divisive drugs can have mid-range means.

Most divisive drugs (≥100 reviews)

Bar = index; right = index · mean rating.

Rank robustness: how sure is each rank?

Head-to-head: is drug A really better than drug B?

Love-or-Hate Index by condition

Conditions with ≥300 reviews. Bubble area ∝ review count; colour = index (blue low, orange high). Conditions where patients disagree most sit highest.

    Validity analysis

    What this system can and cannot claim.

    Supported
    • Descriptive, condition-specific rankings of patient-reported ratings on one platform.
    • Rankings that are more stable for sparsely reviewed drugs (see validation).
    • Transparent uncertainty: review counts, rating histograms and sensitivity to m.
    Not supported
    • Causal effects: no randomisation or counterfactual, so a high rating is not evidence a drug works.
    • Self-selection: people who write reviews are not representative.
    • Confounding: dose, severity, treatment duration and co-medication are unobserved.
    • Review integrity: duplicate or fabricated reviews are possible.
    • Label noise: scraped text contaminated the condition field before cleaning.
    • Drift: reviewer population and platform changed over time.
    • Sparse cells: shrinkage reduces, but does not remove, small-sample bias.

    Run it yourself

    Reproduce every number, then extend it.

    Google Colab / Jupyter notebook

    drug_review_analytics.ipynb loads the raw UCI files (automatic download, or upload archive.zip), cleans them, and reproduces the ranking, funnel, sensitivity, drift and split-half validation, plus a Love-or-Hate index and a true bootstrap rank-robustness analysis.

    colab.research.google.com → File → Upload notebook → Runtime → Run all
    Streamlit app

    The earlier Streamlit version runs the same lookup on the original files.

    pip install streamlit pandas
streamlit run app.py

    Dataset: UCI Drug Review Dataset (Drugs.com). This page is one static file and works offline.
